newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat climbs further as buyers turn sour.
newsitem.headline: French wheat climbs further as buyers turn sour.

text.p: Confident sellers cranked up French wheat cash prices another five francs a tonne on Tuesday in a duel with exporters urgently looking for supplies to meet their order books, dealers said.

Despite an erratic world market, French wheat has been climbing steadily since mid-February as stock holders sense the increasing concern of exporters struggling to catch up with short positions left over from recent sales.
Wheat for March delivery at the northern port of Rouen gained five francs a tonne to trade at 885 francs basis July excluding seasonal carrying charges, dealers said.
Prices for nearby wheat have risen from around 850 francs a tonne on February 12.
Buyers are increasingly unhappy over the rises, which they say make French wheat uncompetitive and may restrict badly needed export licence approvals by the European Commission.
"This is more and more irrational," said one trader, adding the market was looking increasingly helpless as French wheat became around $10 a tonne more expensive than the competition.
The EU increased wheat export approvals last week but agriculture director Guy Legras warned on Monday that domestic prices were already looking too firm at last week's tender.
March wheat at Rouen was quoted around 872.50 francs a tonne at last Thursday's EU export tender.

Although not all grain firms are thought to be short of licences, traders say there is an overall shortage of up to a million tonnes' worth of EU export certificates to cover recent sales of wheat to the Mediterranean basin at lower fob prices.
Exporters have called for an increase in volumes awarded as well as a hike in EU refunds to avert trading losses.
French grain is quoted on a so-called July basis, stripping out the twice-monthly storage premiums payable August onwards during each July/June campaign.
The cumulative premium for wheat delivered in first-half March is 54.53 francs a tonne.
Continued firmness at the ports dragged up prices inland, though feed manufacturers were doing their best to keep this in check by limiting new purchases, dealers said.
Fob Creil wheat for delivery to northern Europe gained 10 francs a tonne to 820 francs for April onwards while fob Moselle wheat added five to 865, they said.
Barley was stable at 855 francs for March or April delivery at Rouen.

Maize, which had risen alongside wheat despite fundamentals seen as weaker, slipped five francs to 855 francs a tonne for delivery to Atlantic ports. But a lack of sellers was putting a floor under prices for the time being, traders said.
Fledgling Matif fob barge wheat futures were unusually active on Tuesday with prices gaining five to six francs a tonne for May through next February on 56 lots by late session.
